SUCA collation

The UCA-equivalent multilevel ordering contract for SuperUnicode strings.

SUCA (SUTS-001) is a full Unicode-UTS-#10-equivalent multilevel collation algorithm over the 64-bit SuperUnicode space. Strings are NFD-normalized, mapped to collation elements (L1–L4 + identical), and compared level by level.

Level Weights Example difference
L1 Base letters role < roles
L2 Accents role < rôle
L3 Case role < Role
L4 Variable (punctuation) interleaving shifted: de-luge ≈ deluge
Identical NFD codepoint tie-break (native codepoint order) deterministic total order
  • Canonical equivalence — normalized input collates equal (e.g. precomposed vs decomposed accents).
  • Contractions — e.g. Slovak c h as a single base letter; expansions — e.g. œ ≈ oe.
  • Variable weighting — shifted (default), blanked, non-ignorable, shift-trimmed; SCP controls are collation-ignorable at L1–L3.
  • Backward secondary — French dictionary order.
  • Implicit weights — unassigned, Han, Native and ExtSUCS plugin codepoints derive algorithmic primaries from the 64-bit codepoint.
  • Tailoring — programmatic rules (& base < x, <<, <<<, =, contractions).

Formalized in SUTR-2 and SUTS-001. Data: collation/SUCA.txt (Base) and collation/ExtUCA.txt (Extended) — both extSUCS-compatible.
